defect.evidence_quote: No negative treatment. *Walder* is the origin of the **impeachment exception** to the exclusionary rule, built on [[Weeks v. United States]] and distinguishing [[Agnello v. United States]]. It was later extended to statements taken in violation of *[[Miranda v. Arizona|Miranda]]* ([[Harris v. New York]]) and to cross-examination reasonably suggested by direct in [[United States v. Havens]], and cabined to the defendant himself (no other defense witnesses) in [[James v. Illinois]].
defect.locator_note: content_page.md Treatment & subsequent history; lake treatment.scope_note and treatment.edges
defect.problem: The core good_law treatment call stands from the lake judgment fields, but the page's 'No negative treatment' phrasing overstates the disclosed treatment record because the same page/lake scope note says Walder was later cabined, and the lake contains proposed negative-signal progeny edges plus audit-needed metadata.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep Treatment: good as of 2026-06-30 and Binding - SCOTUS, but replace 'No negative treatment' with a narrower statement such as: 'No disclosed overruling of Walder's core impeachment-exception holding; later cases extended the doctrine and cabined it to the defendant's own testimony.'

reasons: Lake treatment.field_i_validity is good_law and scope_note says it remains good law, so the status itself is supported.

Lake treatment.derivation records audit_needed true for lane1_negative and lane2_top_cited, with proposed negative events in treatment.edges; that does not defeat good_law, but it makes the no-negative wording too broad.
residual_risks: Because the disclosed derivation has cap_hit/audit_needed metadata, a stronger no-negative claim would require a completed treatment audit not present in the disclosed files.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Say 'good law, later extended and cabined' rather than 'No negative treatment.'
